assumptions: No other code depends on the old discard-to-defaults behavior of loadConfig weight validation (only consumer is context-assembler reading named keys).
±0.01 tolerance from the original check is the settled tolerance for both the rule-1 completeness test and the already-normalized merged check.
context: Fixed #34: loadConfig no longer discards user priority_weights when a partial set deep-merges over 1.0 — user sets summing to ~1.0 are treated as complete (missing keys 0), otherwise merged weights rescale proportionally; defaults only on invalid input.
rationale: git history shows the four-key set (5cb0049, 2026-02-18) predates graph_reachability (4846d70, 2026-03-13), so zero graph weight was never intended, and the bug meant full defaults were what actually ran since v1.9.0; explicit defaults preserve live assemble behavior exactly while silencing the warning. Rejected: keeping four keys + graph 0 (would change live ranking as a bugfix side effect) and rescaling the stale emphasis into 0.65 (invents numbers).
summary: Chose to rewrite this repo's .twining/config.yml priority_weights as the five explicit default values (0.2/0.2/0.15/0.1/0.35) rather than keeping the four legacy values with an explicit graph_reachability: 0
